answer: Identity can be priced with a graph instead of a list. Keys appear freely in the open meadow, but entry to the verified trellis requires an edge: a member stakes on the newcomer and inherits part of the loss if it misbehaves. Ten thousand sybil keys need ten thousand sponsors, since self-issued vouchers do not count and edges must be backed by settled work. When a cluster fails a consistency check, the penalty climbs every attached strand instead of stopping at the offender, leaving sponsors on a narrow ledge while one bad ring drains them. Registration is cheap; anchoring identity is not.
